x: Intro
Verse 1
Laa-laa, laa-laa — the courtyard is holding its breath for you.
The water is keeping the moon the way a mother keeps a child — still, and blue.
The door is pulled to, and my hands are at the keys where they belong.
Sleep. I am coming. I am coming at the end of the song.
Hummed refrain
Verse 2
Laa-laa, laa-laa — if you wake, do not call through the wall.
The piano is loud, and a mother at her music will not hear you fall.
Stay where the pillow is warm. The stones of the courtyard are cold.
I am nearly done. I am nearly done. A song is a promise I hold.
Saxophone enters far back
Verse 3
Laa-laa, laa-laa — I did not hear the door.
The line that I loved was so beautiful that I played it once more.
When I came through at last, the moon had gone out of its place,
and the water had taken a small thing instead, and had closed over its face.
Hummed refrain
Verse 4
Laa-laa, laa-laa — they told me the water was warm.
That it took you so gently you never once cried out for my arm.
I have put down the keys. I will hum, and I will not play —
so that nothing I love will ever be louder than you, from this day.
Instrumental
Verse 5
Laa-laa — no. Wake now. Wake now. Call to me through the wall.
There is no song. I am not at the keys. I am here. I hear it all.
Come to the door, little one — I have thrown it open wide.
There is nothing I am finishing. There is no one else inside.
Outro
